Energy exchange | services = Power trading | revenue = {{down}} {{INRConvert|474|c}} (FY23) | net_income = {{down}} {{INRConvert|305|c}} (FY23){{cite news |title=Indian Energy Exchange Ltd posts Rs. 88.33 crores consolidated PAT in Q4 FY2023 |url=https://www.equitybulls.com/category.php?id=332934 |access-date=27 June 2023 |work=EquityBulls |date=25 May 2023}} | subsidiaries = Indian Gas Exchange | website = {{URL|https://www.iexindia.com/}} }} The '''Indian Energy Exchange''' (IEX){{cite web|url=http://www.iexindia.com |title=Indian Energy Exchange |publisher=Iexindia.com |date= |accessdate=2012-08-08}} is an Indian electronic system based power trading exchange regulated by the [[Central Electricity Regulatory Commission]] (CERC). IEX started its operations on 27 June 2008.{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-first-power-exchange-starts-operations-1174141 |title= First Power Exchange starts operations |publisher=Dnaindia.com |date= |accessdate=2017-02-23}} Indian Energy Exchange pioneered the development of power trading in [[India]] and provides an electronic platform to the various participants in power market, comprising [[State Electricity Board (disambiguation)|State Electricity Board]]s, Power producers ([[GenCos|Gencos]]), Power traders, and Open Access Consumers (both Industrial & Commercial). IEX is one of the two operational Power Exchanges in India. Ever since its incorporation, it has held an influential market share. IEX operates a day-ahead market based on closed auctions with double-sided bidding and uniform pricing;{{cite web|url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/ime/anoops/IEX%20Training-2016/IITK%20-%20PPTs%20-%202016/Day%20-%203%20IITK/Mr.%20Prassana%20Rao%20-%202%20-%20Trading%20at%20Power%20Exchanges.pdf |title= Trading at Power Exchange |publisher=iitk.ac.in |date= |accessdate=2017-02-23}} it has over 3,800 registered clients, over 300 private generators, and more than 3,300 industrial electricity consumers. == Promoters == [[Financial Technologies (India) Limited|63 Moon Technologies Limited]] made an impulsive thrust into India's Power Sector by launching the ''Indian Energy Exchange'' along with [[PTC India]]. The aim of the promoters was to magnify the unexplored potential of the Indian Power market and abridge the demand supply gap. Thereby creating a marketplace wherein players from different purposes may garner business potential. == History == The concept of power exchange in India had its genesis in the year of 2005, post which, Financial Technologies Limited and [[Multi Commodity Exchange]] together yielded an application for setting up the nation's first power exchange. Since its development on 9 June 2008, IEX had recorded 37.4 million transactions, the same month that electricity prices on the exchange hit a record low 13 paisa/KWh. In November 2009, IEX won Best E-Enabled Customer Platform at the second annual India Power Awards for developing what was described as "a robust platform for energy trading.{{cite web|url=http://www.iexindia.com/events/index.htm |title=Indian Energy Exchange |publisher=Iexindia.com |date=2009-11-17 |accessdate=2012-08-08}} == Operations == IEX was envisioned as a neutral platform where participants from different segments of the sector may participate and utilize the range of products and services to match their needs. The participants are required to bear a membership and participate in the bid for the respective product/service. The exchange has launched a range of products and are broadly classified as: Day Ahead, Term Ahead, Renewable Energy Certificates, and Energy Saving Certificates(Es Certs) == Indian Gas Exchange == Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) is a wholly owned subsidiary of IEX, which involves in trading spot and forward contracts of Gas.{{Cite web|title=About Us {{!}} IGX|url=https://www.igxindia.com/about/|access-date=2021-02-24|language=en-US}} The exchange has over 500 registered clients and 15 members. It currently operates from three physical hubs — [[Hazira]], [[Dahej]] and [[Krishna Godavari Basin|KG Basin]].{{Cite news|title=GAIL acquires IEX's 5% stake in Indian Gas Exchange|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/gail-acquires-iexs-5-stake-in-indian-gas-exchange/articleshow/80769305.cms?from=mdr|access-date=2021-03-10}} === Shareholding === Shareholding of IGX as on 10 Mar 2021:{{Cite news|last=Mishra|first=Twesh|date=2021-03-10|title=NSE becomes co-promoter in IGX, buys 26% stake in gas trading hub|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/nse-becomes-co-promoter-in-igx-buys-26-stake-in-gas-trading-hub-121031001089_1.html|access-date=2021-03-10}}{{Cite web|author=Staff Writer|date=2021-03-10|title=ONGC acquires 5% stake in Indian Gas Exchange|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/ongc-acquires-5-stake-in-indian-gas-exchange-11615389619665.html|access-date=2021-03-10|website=mint|language=en}} 26% – [[National Stock Exchange of India]] 5% – [[Oil and Natural Gas Corporation]] 5% – [[Adani Group|Adani Gas]] 5% – [[Torrent Group|Torrent Gas]] 5% – [[GAIL]] Rest – Indian Energy Exchange and other Investors == Controversies == === Insider trading === In October 2025, the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] uncovered a {{INRConvert|173|c}} insider-trading scam involving the IEX. A senior [[Central Electricity Regulatory Commission]] official allegedly leaked confidential market-coupling information to a former student, who profited by trading IEX [[put option]]s before a major share-price drop. SEBI froze the gains and barred the accused from market activity pending further investigation.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2025-10-15 |title=SEBI alleges insider trading of ₹173 crore in IEX |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Economy/sebi-alleges-insider-trading-of-173-crore-in-iex/article70168709.ece |access-date=2025-10-21 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}{{Cite news |last=Shetty |first=Savio |date=16 October 2025 |title=India Regulator Alleges Insider Trading in Energy Bourse Options |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-10-16/india-regulator-alleges-insider-trading-in-energy-bourse-options |access-date=21 October 2025 |work=[[Bloomberg News]]}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Financial services in India}} {{Commodity Exchanges in India}} [[Category:Electric power exchanges]] [[Category:Energy in India]] [[Category:Commodity exchanges in India]] [[Category:Electric power in India]] [[Category:Energy infrastructure in India]] [[Category:2008 establishments in Delhi]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 2008]] [[Category:Companies based in Delhi]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
